issues.failure_explanation: On the square, take v_n(x,y)=exp(n(x-1))cos(ny)e_1. These functions are harmonic, have L-infinity norm 1, and have L2 norm tending to zero. Thus the displayed estimate cannot hold for all H2 functions. The gradient estimates have the same missing boundary restrictions, and expressions involving the L2 norm of ∇Δv are not defined for general H2 functions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use standard estimates in the full H2 and H3 norms, and require H3 whenever ∇Δv is used. Any replacement of full derivatives by Laplacian graph norms needs separately justified boundary hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The unrestricted inequality family cannot justify the auxiliary regularity and contraction estimates as stated.
issues.title: The stated Laplacian-only Sobolev estimates are false without boundary restrictions
issues.why_classification: Standard full-Sobolev-norm estimates provide a local bypass without changing the intended approximation rates; the separate boundary-regularity defects are identified below.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in X does not supply a uniform-in-time W1,infinity bound. More importantly, the H3 calculation explicitly contains second and third derivatives of Φ, which cannot be bounded in terms of ∥∇Φ∥∞ alone. Smooth, rapidly oscillating coefficients can have bounded first derivatives and arbitrarily large higher derivatives. The proof absorbs these quantities into C without an admissible uniform bound or a justified time-integrability estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify coefficient regularity sufficient for the displayed products, retain the higher coefficient norms in the estimate, and justify their time integrability before applying Gronwall.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed uniform auxiliary H3 control, and its intended use to control the iteration, are not established for Φ in X.
issues.title: The auxiliary H3 estimate suppresses necessary coefficient norms
issues.why_classification: This requires a contained regularity estimate and a limited strengthening of the auxiliary coefficient assumptions, rather than merely changing a constant.

issues.failure_explanation: A zero trace of m does not eliminate the boundary terms generated by testing with Δ²m or Δ³m. Even Φ=0 gives a counterexample to the stated uniform H3 estimate without higher compatibility: on the square, u0=x(1-x)y(1-y) has zero trace and belongs to H3, but Δu0 has nonzero boundary trace. The Dirichlet heat solution has Δu(t)=0 on the boundary for t>0, so a uniform H3 bound down to t=0 would contradict trace continuity.

issues.failure_explanation: No domain regularity beyond polygonality is imposed. At a reentrant corner of angle ω, Dirichlet singular functions have the form r^(π/ω)sin(πθ/ω), with exponent below 1; such singularities obstruct the H3/H4 regularity asserted for the auxiliary evolution, even for the scalar heat equation. The later optimal L2 Ritz estimate also needs an adjoint elliptic regularity argument that is unavailable on an arbitrary polygon.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the domain class by explicit primal and adjoint elliptic shift assumptions, or develop corner-domain estimates and revise the affected regularity and convergence claims.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order auxiliary theory and the unrestricted-polygon optimal L2 error claim are unsupported.
issues.title: Arbitrary polygonal domains do not provide the elliptic regularity used
issues.why_classification: The unrestricted polygonal regime must be withdrawn, or substantially different corner-regularity analysis and potentially weaker convergence rates are required.

issues.failure_explanation: The cross-product term is intrinsically skew, not a small discretization asymmetry. On a standard midpoint dual, take constant Φ=e3, u_h=ψ_h e1 and v_h=ψ_h e2. issues.failure_explanation: The intermediate mixed vector (hat m1,m2,m3) is not unit length, yet the damping formula replaces its squared length by 1.
